subject: Limited Liability: proposed language for punitive/incidental carve-out (mutual compromise)
messages:
From: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@nebula-analytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nebula-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines – damages carve-outs

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the order form redline (received yesterday). Our legal team flagged the damages exclusion — specifically the one-way draft that excludes punitive/incidental/consequential damages only for your side. They’ve asked whether Redwood can accept a mutual exclusion or provide clearer examples so we can assess our residual risk.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood agree to mutual language for incidental/consequential/punitive exclusions?
- If not, can you add an express carve-in for (i) gross negligence and (ii) wilful misconduct and (iii) breach of confidentiality obligations?

I’m attaching the SOC2 excerpt we ran by our counsel; they want to ensure the security carve-ins aren’t swallowed by the broad exclusion.

Appreciate your guidance — we’re trying to avoid an extended back-and-forth here.

Rachel
Legal Counsel
Nebula Analytics

Attachment: SOC2-extract.pdf (page references called out in body)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form redlines – damages carve-outs

Marissa / Jonas — pls see note from Nebula. Their counsel pushed back on the one-way exclusion in the order form and wants mutual treatment or explicit carve-ins. I’ve attached their SOC2 excerpt.

Key negotiation points we should consider before I respond:
- Business ask: preserve predictable unit economics / liability cap.
- They want mutuality. We historically push one-way to protect hosted-data exposures.
- Possible compromise: mutual exclusion for incidental/consequential but carve-in for confidentiality breach and gross negligence. For punitive, typical approach is to exclude both ways but allow exceptions for wilful misconduct.

Can you draft a short, plain-English compromise and a legal-friendly redline I can send back this afternoon? I want something that:
1) narrows the definition of consequential/incidental so it isn’t sweeping (use examples),
2) is mutual for incidental/consequential but preserves carve-ins, and
3) confirms punitive damages remain excluded except for wilful misconduct.

Thanks — Olg
Olga Petrov
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_v3-redline.docx (please open the redline tab)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form redlines – damages carve-outs

Thanks Olga — first pass below. Kept the language compact for easier acceptance. Suggest we offer both a short form (for the order form) and a long-form clause (for their counsel).

Short-form proposal (to include in order form):
"Mutual Exclusion of Certain Damages: Except for liability arising from (a) a party's gross negligence, (b) wilful misconduct, or (c) a breach of Confidentiality obligations, neither party shall be liable to the other for incidental, consequential, special, punitive or exemplary damages, including but not limited to loss of profits, loss of business, loss of data, or interruption of business."

Long-form proposal (for MSA redline):
"For the avoidance of doubt, ‘Consequential Damages’ shall not include direct damages reasonably foreseeable from the breach and shall exclude indirect categories such as lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, interruption of business, and third-party claims. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party shall be liable for incidental, consequential, special, punitive or exemplary damages, except to the extent that such liability arises from a party’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of the Data Protection / Confidentiality section, nor shall this exclusion limit either party’s liability for claims brought by third parties to the extent such claims arise from a party’s actionable misconduct."

Question for Jonas — any pushback from Sales on mutuality wording? I tried to be conservative so we don’t expand exposure while signaling compromise.

—Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@nebula-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order form redlines – damages carve-outs

Thanks Marissa — looks good. Two commercial points from my side:
1) If we go mutual on consequential/incidental, we should add a quantifiable cap backstop (order form cap = 12 months of committed fees) so the ask doesn’t materially increase risk.
2) For punitive, make explicit that it is excluded in all circumstances (mutual), except where local law mandates otherwise — e.g., some jurisdictions won’t allow wholesale exclusion for certain statutory penalties.

Suggested combined language (order form level):
"Mutual Limitation & Exclusion: Except to the extent arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, or a party’s breach of Confidentiality obligations, neither party will be liable for incidental, consequential, special, punitive or exemplary damages (including lost profits, loss of business, loss of data, or interruption of business). The total aggregate liability of either party for any and all claims arising out of or in connection with this Order Form shall not exceed the aggregate fees actually paid by Customer under this Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim. Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Section shall limit a party’s liability to the extent such limitation is unenforceable under applicable law."

If you want, I can thread this to their counsel with a 2-sentence commercial rationale: mutuality + cap preserves predictability for both sides and keeps the MSA template consistent across customers.

-Jonas

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Nguyen <rachel.nguyen@nebula-analytics.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@nebula-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Aug 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines – damages carve-outs

Rachel / Tom — thanks for the flag and for sharing the SOC2 note. We discussed internally and think there’s a pragmatic path forward that should address Nebula’s counsel while preserving Redwood’s commercial guardrails.

Proposal we’d like to put on the table (attach both short and long form redlines):
1) Mutual exclusion for incidental/consequential/special/punitive damages, expressly including examples (lost profits, loss of data, business interruption, third-party claims).
2) Carve-ins for: (i) gross negligence, (ii) wilful misconduct, and (iii) breach of Confidentiality/Data Protection obligations.
3) Aggregate cap tied to the Order Form (12 months of paid fees) to keep total exposure bounded.
4) Explicit sentence that statutory or non-waivable liabilities under applicable law are preserved (we cannot contract out of a court-ordered penalty in some jurisdictions).

Why this should work for you: the mutual exclusion gives both parties predictability on indirect damages; the carve-ins and the statutory preservation address the counsel’s SOC2 and data-protection concerns. The cap gives you a tangible recovery floor.

If that sounds acceptable, we’ll circulate an update to the OrderForm_v3-redline.docx and send a single-line cover note for counsel: "We propose the enclosed mutual exclusion with carve-ins and a 12-month cap; this reflects a balanced compromise for both parties."

If you prefer a one-way exclusion instead, we can discuss — but it will require an increased cap or additional indemnity terms to get to parity.

Next step: please confirm by tomorrow EOD and we’ll issue the redlined Order Form and an MSA-level long-form clause for your counsel to review.

Best,
Olg
Olga Petrov
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
